newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPALS -- NY, Ga. deals take center stage.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPALS -- NY, Ga. deals take center stage.

text.p: U.S. municipal bonds were flat to 1/8 point weaker at mid-session as $289 million New York City Municipal Water Finance Authority bonds priced, and JP Morgan Securites Inc reported the account closed on the $240 million Georgia deal it won.
"It's a little easier today just because of the supply and uncertainty in the government market," a municipal trader said.

The U.S. Government market's benchmark 30-year bond was down 7/32 at 101-22/32 to yield 6.50 percent. In addition to municipal supply, traders are eyeing the Treasury's three-part quarterly refunding, which kicks off Tuesday with $16 billion of three-year notes. The bidding deadline is 1300 EDT.
Back in municipals, one trader said roughly $200 million of bid wanted lists were circulating as players made way for new product. He described that amount as "moderate."
In debt futures, the September municipal contract was down 6/32 at 120-8/32. The September T-bond was down 6/32 at 114-15/32. The MOB spread was 185 ticks.

Traders said the New York City water deal was grabbing much of the market's focus. PaineWebber Inc tentatively priced the $289 million bonds at a top yield of 5.474 percent in 2021. The top maturity in 2022 was Ambac Assurance Corp-insured, and was priced to yield 5.35 percent. The deal was scaled back from $365 million.

"City Water looks like it's going to have to be repriced to get the institutional business that it needs to get it done," one trader said. "I think it's a little high. It's a little pricey where they've got it right now, so we expect to see that repriced."
If the deal offers five basis points more yield, it will get done, he said.
The City Water deal aside, new issues were "properly priced" overall, the trader said.
"New deals are being priced competitively, and (are) being well received," he said.

On the competitive side, JP Morgan won the $240 million Georgia bonds at a net interest cost of 4.7584 percent. The sale went off at 1100 EDT and JP Morgan reported the account closed by 1220 EDT. The deal is rated triple-A by Moody's Investors Service, Standard & Poor's Corp and Fitch Investors Service.

"With the back up in the market from last Thursday, plus the fact that they are triple-triples, plus the fact that they are non-callable and it's a very popular name, the deal sold out very quickly," JP Morgan Managing Director Peter Clarke said.
Elsewhere in negotiated action, Siebert Brandford Shank & Co tentatively priced $244 million Detroit, Mich., water supply system revenue bonds at a top yield of 5.45 percent in 2027.
Smith Barney Inc restructured $227 million Austin, Texas, combined utility systems revenue refunding bonds. The top yield after the restructuring remained 5.43 percent in 2020.
Goldman Sachs & Co tentatively priced $115 million New York State Environmental Facilities Corp bonds at a top yield of 5.38 percent in 2019.
Bear Stearns & Co tentatively priced $78 million Illinois Housing Development Authority bonds at a top yield of 5.8 percent in 2028.
PaineWebber Inc tentatively priced $74 million Arkansas Development Finance Authority bonds at a top yield of 5.8 percent in 2030.
